blocks.text: The start sort is O(n log n). Across the scan, every meeting end is pushed once and removed at most once. Each heap operation costs O(log n), so all heap work is O(n log n), not O(n^2). If all meetings overlap, no end is released before the last start and the heap stores n values, giving O(n) extra space. A two-array method also uses O(n) storage when endpoint arrays are copied, while an in-place representation may account differently. The key is to derive cost from active-state size, not from the visual presence of one loop.

feedback.reason: Sorting costs O(n log n), and each meeting performs at most one heap push and one eventual pop, each O(log n); the heap can grow to n.
